subhead: Driven notably by Rafale fighter jet sales to India and missile exports, France exported €21.2 billion worth of arms in 2025, matching its 2024 total.

Kremlin cracks down on all anti-war voices ahead of Russia's elections
subhead: Lev Shlosberg, one of the few Russian opposition figures to publicly denounce the offensive in Ukraine while remaining in Russia, has been sentenced to more than 11 years in prison. His party, the only anti-war political group, has been barred from the September 20 election.

title: French PM asks ministers to clamp down on corruption in civil service
subhead: Sébastien Lecornu urged his government to step up its vigilance against integrity violations in public administrations and to intensify disciplinary action, amid rising drug trafficking and cybercrime.

title: Meta's trial challenges the greed of tech platforms
subhead: Twenty-nine US states have taken legal action against Mark Zuckerberg's company, Meta. This trial signals a crucial societal wake-up call, reminiscent of the shift in public opinion against tobacco giants 30 years ago.

title: Two years after Paris Olympics, Wembanyama returns as French national team captain
subhead: Victor Wembanyama will play his first game with France since the national team's loss to the US in the 2024 Olympics final on Thursday, facing Serbia. The San Antonio Spurs center is taking on new responsibilities in a significantly revised squad.

Mahmoud Darwish and Tamar Ben Ami: The impossible love of a Palestinian poet and an Israeli dancer
subhead: In the early 1960s, in Haifa, Israel, the young Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish fell in love with Tamar Ben Ami, a Jewish Israeli dancer. Their romance was intense but brief. From this forbidden love, the writer composed a poignant poem, 'Rita and the Rifle,' which is still sung throughout the Arab world.

title: Jean Hegland, American novelist: 'The idea that humans must dominate the Earth and animals has not served us well'
subhead: In an interview with Le Monde, the author of the cult novel 'Into the Forest' calls for thinking beyond infinite growth, which she sees as incompatible with protecting the living world.

title: Why Le Pen's plan for a constitutional referendum would be 'a coup d'état in form and content'
subhead: If she were to win, far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has pledged to call a referendum to revise the Constitution and enshrine the far right's core principles in it. According to a member of the highest administrative court, this would be 'a double coup d'état, both in form and content.'
